draft.title: The end of the Western Roman Empire
card: In the later 300s CE the Roman Empire was split into a western half and an eastern half, each with its own emperor. The western half was ruled from Italy and the eastern half from Constantinople.
it ended in 476 CE, when a Germanic general, Odoacer, removed the last western emperor. Its lands in western Europe were then ruled by new kingdoms.
it kept going for almost 1000 more years. It ended in 1453 CE, when the Ottomans captured Constantinople.
Much of Rome's world did not vanish. Roman law shaped later legal systems, Latin grew into languages such as Italian, French and Spanish, and Christianity stayed strong.
draft.remember: Only the western half fell in 476 CE. The eastern half lasted to 1453, and Roman law, language and religion carried on.

a.q: Which statement about the Roman Empire is correct?
opts: The west ended in 476 CE and the east lasted to 1453
The east ended in 476 CE and the west lasted to 1453
Both halves ended in 476 CE, when Odoacer took power
Both halves lasted to 1453, when the Ottomans won
a.why: The western half ended in 476 CE, but the eastern half lasted until the Ottomans captured Constantinople in 1453. The tempting option that says both halves ended in 476 CE treats the whole empire as one, but only the western half fell then.
a.clue: The empire had two halves, and they ended at different times.

b.q: A student says, "When Rome fell in 476 CE, everything Roman disappeared from Europe." Which reply is best?
opts: Roman law, Latin and Christianity carried on after 476 CE
Only the Eastern Empire ended in 476 CE, not the Western
Latin disappeared in 476 CE, but Roman law carried on
Roman rule ended in the east in 476 CE, but not the west
b.why: Roman law shaped later legal systems, Latin grew into several languages, and Christianity stayed strong. Only the western empire's rule ended in 476 CE, so the claim that everything vanished is wrong. The option saying Latin disappeared is tempting, but Latin lived on in languages such as Italian and French.
b.clue: Think about what carried on after the western emperor was removed.

wants.brief: A map of the Roman Empire in the later 300s CE, showing the western half ruled from Italy and the eastern half ruled from Constantinople, with the dividing line between them labelled.
wants.why: It shows the empire's two halves so students can see why one could fall while the other lasted.

a.best: The west ended in 476 CE and the east lasted to 1453

b.best: Roman law, Latin and Christianity carried on after 476 CE
